acceptanceResults.criterion: Every seam surface is checked against three questions: does it degrade when the service is absent, does it sanitize/limit anything it renders from untrusted state, and does it clean up on unload (ctx.effect) — with a finding for each violation.
acceptanceResults.evidence: See seamMatrix: all 9 seams degrade honestly (absent/refused/requested states, never a false confirmed); every rendered value passes sanitize.ts before the host's own cleanRenderText; cleanup is host-bound (bindCallerEffect in all six dsh-TUI seam modules) — verdict-bearing findings R1 (unguarded grant accessor) and R2 (harness-side registrations not releasable by the plugin) are recorded, and the naive 'discarded disposer = leak' reading is explicitly refuted.

acceptanceResults.criterion: The ready-but-not-activated decision-event seam is checked for honest behaviour: no test-token or bypass path, a single warning, and no claim of activation anywhere in code, docs or manifest.
acceptanceResults.evidence: No token/bypass: the only 'token' hits in src/ and test/ are comments explaining that admission is token-gated and unreachable and that the plugin never calls admit/admitInternal (decisions.ts:5-7,21-22). Single warning: log.warn fires once per boot for the whole seam, not per event (decisions.ts:122-128). No activation claim: README.md:28,99 and decisions.ts:1-3 say ready-but-NOT-activated; dsh-plugin.json x-mpd-tui-surfaces.decisionEvents states 'built ready-but-not-activated, never faked'; the ACTIVE log line is reachable only when grants.allows() === true (decisions.ts:119).

acceptanceResults.criterion: The review explicitly states what it could not verify and why.
acceptanceResults.evidence: notVerified below: the host-internal renderer mechanism, dynamic reload behaviour, the multi-session workspace-ordering hazard (not reachable in the single-session TUI composition), and whether the multi-anchor dsh-session resolution covers every future copy.

findings.problem: `const facade = host.grants` reads a host GETTER outside any try/catch. The installed host's getter calls hostStateFor(this), which THROWS 'tuiPluginHost host state is unavailable' on a state-map miss (plugin-host.js:633-637 — the same failure class as the renderer facade). onService then swallows the exception (host.ts:100), so the seam leaves its INITIAL outcome in place: {state:'absent', detail:'tuiPluginHost was not injected'} — a FALSE cause, since tuiPluginHost was in fact injected.
findings.consequence: Diagnostics-only, and the safety property still holds (nothing is reported confirmed/ACTIVE). But the honesty requirement this seam was repaired for is violated on that path: the disclosure names the wrong reason, and attempts() stays empty.
findings.requiredFix: Wrap the facade read in try/catch and set `granted = undefined` on a throw; the existing branch for undefined already reports the honest `requested` / 'grant state not queryable in this composition'.

findings.problem: The two HARNESS-side registrations are not releasable by the plugin. dsh-settings.register binds its effect to the SERVICE's own ctx (`this.ctx.effect(...)`, dsh-settings/lib/types/index.js:244-248) and returns an owner HANDLE (get/watch/update/replace) — there is no disposer for us to own. dsh-commands.register returns a disposer created with `this.layers.effect(this.ctx, ...)` (dsh-commands/lib/index.js:257-260), also service-bound; commands.ts:54 discards it.
findings.consequence: After a plugin unload/hot-reload the /mpd command and the mpd settings namespace survive; re-registering the namespace then THROWS 'settings namespace "mpd" is already registered' (dsh-settings index.js:229-231), which our catch reports as `refused` — i.e. the settings seam degrades on reload rather than re-activating. Bounded (no data loss, no boot failure) but worth disclosing.
findings.requiredFix: Disclose the reload behaviour in README (and/or the manifest), or probe-then-skip when the namespace already exists. Note the contrast that must NOT be misread: every dsh-TUI seam service DOES self-bind the caller effect, so discarding THOSE disposers is safe — see verifiedNonFindings.

findings.problem: `workspaceRootsAll()[0]` returns the FIRST live session workspace, which is order-dependent when a host serves several sessions with different workspaces (AGENTS.md §6 warns that the session fact must win over process-wide state). The plugin is agentless and cannot select the current session.
findings.consequence: Not reachable in the shipped composition — a dsh-tui process owns one session, and my t8 run proves the resolution read the SANDBOX workspace (status line 'mpd: team - · plans 0') rather than the repo's real board (11 members / 3 plans). On a multi-session host the board could project another session's state.
findings.requiredFix: Prefer the TUI's own workspace source (the host resolves config.workspace ?? DSH_TUI_WORKSPACE_TARGET) when available, falling back to the current order; or document the single-session assumption.

findings.problem: `probeDecisionEvents?()` is declared and never called anywhere in src/ (grep: declaration only), so an available host read-back for the DecisionEvents feature is unused. `confirmed` therefore rests on grants.allows() === true plus a non-throwing subscribe.
findings.consequence: Diagnostics-only. The strongest available honest signal IS already used (the grant facade, per the t23 repair), so no false claim results; the residual is that a second confirming source exists and is not consulted.
findings.requiredFix: Optional: call probeDecisionEvents() where present and fold it into the seam detail, so `confirmed` has two independent witnesses.

findings.problem: t10-F3 residual: `confirm()` is typed Promise<boolean | undefined> while the host always resolves a boolean (dialogs.ts:363-364 resolves boolean; :373 and :393-395 return false).
findings.consequence: Harmless widening — the caller treats undefined as cancel, which is the same visible behaviour.
findings.requiredFix: Optional: narrow the type to Promise<boolean> and keep the runtime guard.

verifiedNonFindings.claim: Discarding the disposer returned by tuiScenes / tuiSettingsSections / tuiCommandTrees register() leaks the registration on unload.
verifiedNonFindings.refuted: The host binds the caller effect ITSELF for every dsh-TUI seam service — bindCallerEffect is present in scenes.ts (3), settings-sections.ts (3), command-trees.ts (2), shortcuts.ts (2), status.ts (4) and renderers.ts (2) — so a plugin-scoped registration is released when that scope's activation unloads. Our extra effectOn ownership on status/shortcuts/renderers/decisions is belt-and-braces, not the only cleanup path. Recorded so a later reader does not file this as a false positive.

verifiedNonFindings.claim: t10-F1 (ACTIVE inferred from the disposer's type) still ships.
verifiedNonFindings.refuted: CLOSED at the current revision. decisions.ts keys on the grant facade (grants.allows === true) for `confirmed`, treats a non-function return as a hard refusal, never calls a disposer as a probe, and covers the `() => false` sentinel with a test ('a missing decision grant with a no-op disposer is refused, and the disposer is not called as a probe').

CLOSED. shortcuts.ts uses the host's list() read-back for confirmation (refused when none of our bindings appear) and describes the disposer as 'NOT proof of registration'; renderers.ts counts requests and reports `requested` with the explicit 'a refusal also returns a disposer' caveat.

Guarded by tests that MODEL the host: a ctx without inject registers nothing even when get() would answer, a ctx with inject but no composed service registers nothing and throws nothing, and the suite grew 29 → 37 tests with the repair. bun test exits 0 with 37 pass / 0 fail.

verifiedNonFindings.claim: Untrusted state could reach the render path unsanitized.
verifiedNonFindings.refuted: Every value read from team.json / boulder.json / plan names / workmate meta flows through sanitize.ts (scalars only, C0/C1 stripped — which also defuses ANSI/CSI — whitespace collapsed, cell-clamped with wide-glyph awareness, bounded line counts), and the host sanitizes again with cleanRenderText.

verifiedNonFindings.claim: The plugin writes state (which could escape the workspace or touch ~/.dsh).
verifiedNonFindings.refuted: grep for writeFileSync/appendFileSync/mkdirSync/rmSync/unlinkSync/createWriteStream over src/ returns nothing: the package is read-only. registration.ts only reads profile directories; state.ts only reads.

verifiedNonFindings.claim: The /mpd command is unattributed in the effect ledger (t10-F4).
verifiedNonFindings.refuted: Not a defect — an admitted Component is required for the mediated tuiPluginHost.registerCommand path, and admission is `waiting_authorization` by design. The consequence (ledger rows as `undeclared`) is MEASURED and DISCLOSED in dsh-plugin.json x-mpd-tui-surfaces.decisionEvents.

notVerified: The host-internal cause of the renderer projection gap (H1 vs H2 from t8): the host checkout is read-only and exposes no registration read-back, so the two readings remain indistinguishable. Not a property of this package either way.

Dynamic reload behaviour of R2 was NOT executed (no reload harness in this wave): the consequence is derived from the installed services' own source (effect bound to the service ctx; duplicate namespace THROWS).
The R3 multi-session hazard is unreachable in the shipped single-session TUI composition and was therefore not exercised.

Whether the multi-anchor dsh-session resolution in registration.ts reaches EVERY copy that a future harness generation uses for its strict read paths (it probes import.meta.url, argv[1] and every <home>/profiles/*/package.json); the append is skipped unless one copy VERIFIES the type, so the failure mode is a skipped record, never a corrupt session.
